pool.text: The city of Seville surrendered to Ferdinand III after fifteen months of siege.
The first tribunal of the Spanish Inquisition was instituted in Seville.
Seville was chosen as headquarters of the Casa de Contratación.
The Great Plague of Seville reduced the population by almost half.
The first newspaper in Spain outside Madrid began publication in Seville.
King Ferdinand VII granted a Royal Document for support against the French invasion
The city hosted the Ibero-American Exposition, creating new public spaces.
Seville fell very quickly at the beginning of the Spanish Civil War.
General Francisco Franco honored the city for its devotion to the Virgin Mary
The shipyard of Seville was opened, employing many workers.
Seville was declared a disaster zone due to severe river floods.
Spain held its first democratic municipal elections after the dictatorship.
Pope John Paul II arrived in Seville to officiate at a Mass.
Teresa Sánchez López won the title of Miss National in the contest
The Universal Exposition was held for six months in Seville.
Eva Maria González became the beauty queen and model who was Miss España
The Metropol Parasol project was launched to revitalise the Plaza de la Encarnación.
The Seville Metro began operating its transportation service in the city.
The city council provided a grant to create the Science Centre.
The Metropol Parasol was completed, costing more than originally planned.
